justification: Explicitly a review of cannabis pharmacology relying on animal models for memory effects, not a primary human study.
Observational human study linking marijuana use to worse verbal learning and delayed recall via CogState list task.
Explicitly a meta-analysis and systematic review of cannabinoid-1 receptor compounds on memory across species.
Meta-analysis of neurocognition in cannabis-using psychosis patients, not a primary empirical study.
Experimental crossover THC study in healthy males using fMRI during verbal learning/encoding task.
Longitudinal study of adolescent cannabis use and neurocognitive change including working/short-term memory measures.
Exposure studied is binge drinking; cannabis frequency only a covariate, not a characterized cannabis exposure examined against memory.
Human study of synthetic cannabinoid users assessed on n-back working memory and free-recall long-term memory tasks.
Cross-sectional study comparing heavy cannabis users vs non-users on neurocognitive battery including episodic memory.
Proposes a research agenda and treatment strategy for marijuana addiction; not a primary empirical study.
Observational study of adolescent cannabis use and cognition using CANTAB spatial working memory and learning measures.
Naturalistic follow-up characterizing cannabis/substance use with spatial working memory outcomes in first-episode schizophrenia.
